power.summary:
ESCs (4-6S, standard PWM). The cheapest credible option is the genuine-branded Hobbywing SkyWalker V2 on AliExpress. Prices are logged out, with the strikethrough 'original' prices ignored:
- 60A V2: KRW 37,600 + 4,347 shipping (FPV Hub) or KRW 37,700 + 4,287 (SkyTech). 60/80A, 3-6S, 5V/7A BEC, 68 g, 73x30x12 mm.
- 80A V2: KRW 44,600 + 4,287 (SkyTech). 80/100A, 3-6S, 5V/7A BEC, 79 g, 85x36x9 mm.
- 100A V2: KRW 51,300 with free shipping. 100/120A, 92 g.

The SkyWalker V2 default throttle range is 1100-1940 us and can be calibrated to the transmitter, so 50 Hz PWM from the ATmega128 is fine. All numbers come from the Hobbywing manufacturer table. The same 80A from a Korean seller costs KRW 60,100 on 11st with next-day delivery. Hobbywing Direct sells the 80A for USD 44.99 (KRW 60,318) but does not list Korea for shipping. Cheaper alternatives are the Surpass Flier 80A at KRW 42,000 (specs unverified) and the ZTW Beatles G2 80A at KRW 53,440 regular (8A SBEC, about 92 g, per a retailer).

LiPos. The cheapest credible source is CNHL's own site, which lists KR for its Global warehouse. Shipping is from USD 6.99 (KRW 9,372) and free over USD 79; transit is 15-20 working days.
- G+Plus 6S 2200 70C XT60: USD 29.99 (KRW 40,207), 349 g, 109x35x51 mm.
- G+Plus 4S 2200 70C XT60: USD 43.98 per 2-pack (KRW 29,482 each), 250 g, 106x35x38 mm.
- G+Plus 4S 3000 70C XT90: USD 36.99 (KRW 49,593), 323 g.
- G+Plus 6S 4000 70C XT90: USD 60.99 (KRW 81,769), 611 g.

All CNHL figures are manufacturer specs. On AliExpress, the Ovonic Rebel 110C 4S 2200 is KRW 33,100 and the 6S 2600 is KRW 44,800, but weights are not shown and the slow '기타' shipping is estimated to arrive 13 Dec. Korean 11st sellers ask KRW 62,000-80,000 for a 4S or 6S 2200 pack.

Charger. The cheapest option is an iMAX B6AC 80W clone on AliExpress at KRW 31,400 with free shipping; it has a built-in AC supply, so no PSU is needed, but no KC info is given. In Korea, the same type is KRW 44,300 on 11st with next-day delivery. The genuine SkyRC B6AC V2 costs KRW 84,887 + 11,555 shipping (AC built in, 50W, 6A, 1-6S, 632 g). Its 50W limit means only about 2A charging on 6S. The ISDT 608AC costs KRW 84,733 + 7,111 and includes a detachable AC brick (AC 50W / DC 200W, 8A). The ToolkitRC M7 at KRW 57,200 is DC-only (7-28V, 200W, 10A) and needs a separate PSU.

Cheapest credible propulsion-electronics set:
- 80A ESC: about KRW 48,900 shipped.
- One CNHL 6S 2200 70C: about KRW 49,600 shipped. With 2 packs plus other items above USD 79, shipping becomes free.
- B6AC clone charger: KRW 31,400.
The total is about KRW 130,000, before the EDF, servos and airframe.

Korean prices therefore come only from 11st, plus one Danawa search-page listing that was not used.

Freewing/FMS 80A ESC: USD 49.99 comes only from a search snippet (the Motion RC page returned 404). Its BEC rating and weight are not listed.
Flycolor ESCs were not checked. Ultra-cheap generic 80-100A ESCs (KRW 4,000-19,000 new-member prices) were skipped as not credible.

No official Korean customs or KC rule about importing LiPo was found. Observed facts: several AliExpress LiPo listings ship only by the slow '기타' method (estimated delivery 13 Dec 2026), while the GNB listing and all ESC listings use standard 19-26 Oct. CNHL explicitly lists KR in its Global warehouse shipping countries. Hobbywing Direct does not list South Korea. FedEx and DHL treat standalone lithium batteries as dangerous goods (FedEx: standalone Li-ion shipped at no more than 30% state of charge) (https://www.fedex.com/ko-kr/shipping-guide/pack/lithium-batteries.html, https://mydhl.express.dhl/kr/ko/help-and-support/shipping-advice/what-can-i-ship/lithium-batteries.html). One US shop (Pyrodrone) is reported in search results as not shipping batteries outside the US; this is unverified.
The ZTW Beatles G2 80A specs come from a single retailer (OZ Robotics); BuddyRC lists a different, older 'Beatles 80A' with a 3A BEC.
The ISDT 608AC weight (350 g) comes from one retailer, and its dimensions were not found. Listings disagree on AC power (50W vs 60W).
A DC power supply for DC-only chargers (ToolkitRC M7) was not priced.
The Lindinger EUR 39.99 price for the SkyWalker 80A V2 was not converted (no EUR rate was fetched).
CNHL shipping cost to KR is given as 'from USD 6.99'. The actual quote for a battery-only order was not checked, because that needs a cart or checkout and I did not use one.

A 70mm unit in the same thread went from 178 g to 148 g with the housing off; that it was the Powerfun is my inference. Thrust per 10,000 KRW: 6S 395.8 g (358.5 g including shipping); 4S 304 g at the rated 1640 g, or 315 g at the measured 1.70 kg. Another Powerfun listing, https://ko.aliexpress.com/item/1005010412107169.html, is more expensive: 4S KRW 70,400, 6S KRW 73,900, plus KRW 8,196 shipping and a 14-day dispatch time.

edf.summary:
This covers EDF units only (fan + motor), with prices read on 2026-10-13 at 1 USD = 1,341.49 KRW. The best value is a 70mm 12-blade unit on 6S: the Hobbyocean 70mm 2300KV on AliExpress is KRW 35,900 with free shipping and a regular store price, not a new-member-only deal. Its thrust is only a title claim of about 2,200 g with no voltage or current, which works out to about 613 g per 10,000 KRW.

**Cheapest credible option per size**
- **70mm (recommended class):**
  - Hobbyocean 70mm 2300KV, as above. A related Powerfun 70mm table lists 2,240 g at 25.2 V / 65 A / 1,638 W and 178 g total. The same Hobbyocean listing has a 4S 3400KV version for KRW 36,600, and the 2300KV bundled with an 80A ESC is KRW 72,600.
  - The Powerfun-branded 70mm costs KRW 53,900 (4S) or KRW 56,600 (6S), plus KRW 5,874 shipping. Vendor figures: 4S 1,640 g at 62 A; 6S 2,240 g at 65 A.
  - This is the only cheap unit with an independent test: a Powerfun 70mm 3400KV on 4S averaged 1.70 kg against a 1.81 kg rating (Rocketry Forum EDF rocketry thread). That suggests vendor claims for this family are about 6% optimistic.
- **64mm:**
  - The cheapest unit with published thrust is the Powerfun/Hobbyocean 64mm 11-blade 4S 3500KV, vendor-rated 1,460 g at 52 A / 874 W and 150 g. Search cards show about KRW 35-43k, but I could not confirm which variant those prices are for.
  - Independent 64mm 3S/4S tests (brands not named) measured 1.07-1.38 kg on 4S.
  - QX-MOTOR's 64mm QF2822 is about KRW 39k at the new-member price. The regular price is not shown, and no thrust is published for the KVs on sale.
  - XFLY 64mm costs KRW 65,615 for fan + motor, with an unverified 1,250 g, so it is poor value.
- **80mm:** FMS 80mm 3280-KV2100 at KRW 115,899 (AliExpress, free shipping), vendor-rated 3,500 g at 25 V / 98 A and 300 g, about 302 g per 10k KRW. It needs a 100A+ ESC.
- **90mm:** Hobbyocean 90mm 6S 1450KV at KRW 83,400 with free shipping. Using the Powerfun 90mm table as a stand-in: 3.09 kg at 22.2 V / 102 A, or 3.79 kg at 25.2 V / 124 A, and 369 g. That gives about 370-454 g per 10k KRW.
  - It needs a 120A ESC and a 6S pack that can deliver over 100 A.
  - The lip is Ø112 mm and the mounting tabs span 114.2 mm, which may not fit a Ø110 body.

**What this means for the 200-300k KRW budget**
- A 70mm 6S Hobbyocean unit with its 80A ESC (KRW 72,600) leaves the most room for batteries, servos and printing.
- A 90mm unit costs KRW 83-115k before a 120A ESC and a high-current 6S pack.
- The branded alternatives (FMS, Freewing, JP Hobby, Dynam) cost KRW 59-241k. Most of their pages publish no thrust; the exceptions are JP Hobby 70mm (2,350 g at 22.2 V for KRW 241k), Freewing 80mm (3.7 kg, about KRW 149k) and Dynam 64mm (1,800 g at 70 A, sold out).
gaps: No Korean domestic listing was found: searches for Coupang, 11st, Naver smartstore and Korean RC shops (헬리하우스, 프로헬기, rcbank) returned nothing. Every price here is from an overseas shop.

AliExpress product descriptions did not load because of an anti-bot check. On one product page (Hobbyocean 64mm, item 1005007031481465) a CAPTCHA appeared. I did not solve it and stopped browsing AliExpress. Specs therefore come from gallery images, titles, or Banggood/manufacturer tables.

AliExpress KR pages viewed without logging in show one-time new-member prices (신규 회원 전용 혜택가) for the QX-MOTOR and XFLY listings. Regular prices for a buyer who is not a new member are not shown, and the crossed-out 'original' prices (up to 3.4x higher) may not be real prices.
The Powerfun 64mm (KRW 43,000) and Hobbyocean 64mm (KRW 35,431) prices come from search-result cards. I could not confirm which variant (fan only or with motor) they are for.

No published thrust was found for: QX-MOTOR 64mm QF2822 2100/2300/3300/4300KV; QX 70mm QF2827 and QF3027; FMS official 64mm 2840-KV3150, 70mm 3060-KV1900 and 90mm 3670-KV1950; Freewing 64mm and 70mm systems; Freewing 80mm 3530-1680KV.

Hobbyocean thrust is only the title claim of about 2,200 g (70mm), with no voltage or current, or nothing at all (90mm). Powerfun tables are used as a stand-in, but I have not confirmed that the two brands sell the same product. The Powerfun 70mm table lists '6S 2400KV' while listings say 2300KV.

Independent thrust tests were found only for the Powerfun 70mm 3400KV on 4S (1.70 kg measured vs 1.81 kg rated), several unbranded 64mm 3S/4S units on 4S (1.07-1.38 kg), and an unidentified 70mm 12-blade unit in an Indonesian thesis (2,061.7 g at 1,600 W vs 2,250 g claimed, -8.4%). None was found for the cheap 80mm or 90mm units, or for QX-MOTOR or XFLY.

Most listings do not state rotation direction, inner duct diameter, overall length, or whole-unit weight. The exceptions are the drawings for the Hobbyocean 70mm and 90mm and the JP Hobby and Dynam figures.
eBay pages (for example a Powerfun 70mm 6S at USD 44.99 + USD 6.52 shipping, seen only in a search snippet) returned HTTP 403, so they are not included.
Banggood pages did not render prices (US$00.00 placeholders), and most EDF items said they cannot ship to Korea. Banggood was used only for spec tables.
Motion RC prices are displayed without a decimal point (e.g. '$4699'). I read them as USD 46.99 and so on; Freewing 80mm appears at two prices ($95.49 and $110.99).
Shipping to Korea from FMS, Motion RC and Dynam is not shown, and import duties are not included.
The exchange rate is a EUR cross rate from Banque de France (2026-10-09). I found no direct USD/KRW quote for 2026-10-12 or 10-13 from a single source.

electronics.summary:
Prices were read 2026-10-13; FX is 1 USD = 1,340.71 KRW. AliExpress showed prices in KRW to a non-logged-in visitor from Korea. Where it showed a one-time new-user deal, I used the regular (struck-through) price and put the new-user price in notes.

Cheapest credible option per category:
- **ATmega128 board:** Korea: DeviceMart LK LA9 at 33,000 KRW incl. VAT; LA22 breadboard module 44,000. AliExpress minimum-system board ₩8,735 + ₩1,953 shipping; the crystal is not specified and one buyer got 8 MHz.
- **MPU-6050 GY-521:** DeviceMart 4,950 KRW; AliExpress ₩2,572 with free shipping.
- **Barometers:**
  - BMP280: DeviceMart 2,200 KRW, AliExpress ₩2,180. Noise is only a vendor claim (Adafruit: 0.25 m altitude noise, ±1 hPa).
  - MS5611 GY-63: Mechasolution 18,700 KRW; AliExpress XRY ₩4,780 + ₩1,973. Datasheet resolution is 0.012 mbar at OSR 4096 (about 10 cm).
  - BMP388: AliExpress diymore ₩7,140; DeviceMart DFRobot 12,540. Bosch: 0.03 Pa noise, ±0.08 hPa relative.
  - BMP390: DFRobot BMP390L 20,350 KRW (sold out); AliExpress about ₩10,954. Bosch page: 0.02 Pa RMS noise, ±0.03 hPa relative (about ±25 cm), 200 Hz.
- **4-channel level shifter:** Mechasolution 2,650 KRW (FET not named); Adafruit BSS138 #757 at DeviceMart 7,920 KRW (2-week lead time); AliExpress ₩344 + ₩1,417.
- **3.3 V LDO:** Mechasolution AMS1117 module 660 KRW (4.5-7 V in, 800 mA).
- **MG90S:**
  - Korea: icbanq TowerPro 2,860 KRW each, so 14,300 KRW for 5.
  - AliExpress: 5-pack ₩13,932 with free shipping.
  - TowerPro table: 13.4 g, 1.8 kgf·cm at 4.8 V and 2.2 kgf·cm at 6.6 V, 0.10 s/60° at 4.8 V and 0.08 s/60° at 6 V. Clones are unverified.
- **UBEC:**
  - 6 V servo rail: RCbank Hobbywing 5/6 V 3 A (5 A for 30 s) at 16,500 KRW, input 5.5-23 V. That is below a full 6S pack's 25.2 V.
  - 5 V logic rail: RCbank UBEC-3A at 4,800 KRW, input 5.5-26 V per its spec table, inconsistent with its 5-23 V title.
  - DeviceMart interboard 5 V 3 A, 7-40 V input (2-8S), 11,760 KRW.
  - AliExpress 5/6 V 3 A ₩2,256 + ₩1,940; HENGE 5/6 V 6-8 A (12 A max) ₩11,637 + ₩3,466.
  - 12S input: 20 A 2-12S SBEC ₩22,436 (no 6 V output); UBEC-YL12S5A 8-12S 5 A ₩30,800.
- **Logging:**
  - OpenLog clone on AliExpress ₩3,980 with free shipping, vs genuine SparkFun at DeviceMart 42,900 KRW.
  - Plain SPI microSD module: DeviceMart 1,100 KRW (level shifting not stated) or AliExpress level-shifted ₩1,142 + ₩2,297.
- **RC:** No FS-i6X found at reachable Korean shops.
  - AliExpress i6X + iA6B: ₩117,957 regular / ₩77,061 new-user (500+ sold), or ₩70,500 from a 4-sold listing.
  - Korean FlySky FS-i6 sets: 142,000 KRW at RCbank.
  - Cheapest SBUS receiver: FS-A8S V2 on AliExpress, ₩9,959 + ₩1,871. In Korea: FS-iA6B (S-BUS) 31,000 KRW at RCbank.
- **USBasp:** DeviceMart SZH-PRBF-007 at 4,400 KRW.
- **Consumables:**
  - Bambu PLA Matte from the official KR store: refill ₩18,000/kg (₩15,300 each when buying 4), with spool ₩22,000, free shipping over ₩70k. No cheaper credible PLA found; Woorim PLA is 15,500 + 3,000 shipping.
  - Recovery: AliExpress 100 cm parachute ₩23,234, 150 cm ₩38,847, material unstated. Ripstop 1 x 1.5 m for DIY ₩3,151-7,602 with free shipping.
  - Fasteners: DeviceMart M3 bolt + nut kit, 340 pcs, 9,680 KRW.
  - Connectors and wire (RCbank): Amass XT60H 1,800 KRW; XT90 2 pairs 4,000 KRW; 12 AWG silicone 1 m + 1 m 6,000 KRW.

**Basket:** DeviceMart ships free at 66,000 KRW or more. LA9 + MPU-6050 + BMP280 + SD module + USBasp + M3 kit + interboard UBEC comes to about 67,090 KRW, so one order clears the threshold.

**Rough Korea-sourced flight-electronics total, excluding RC and filament:** about 105-125k KRW. That is DeviceMart about 67k, RCbank UBECs + connectors + wire about 33k + 3.5k shipping, 5 MG90S 14.3k, and Mechasolution parts about 3.3k.

**Doing the same with AliExpress:** about 40-50k KRW, plus 3-5 weeks of shipping.

**RC is the biggest single item:** about 77-118k KRW from AliExpress, or 142k+ in Korea. Borrowing a transmitter would save the most.
gaps: FS-i6X with a receiver was not found at any Korean shop I could reach. Naver Shopping is blocked in the browser, Gmarket showed a bot check, and Coupang was not reachable. The only Korean FlySky sets found are FS-i6 at RCbank (142,000 KRW and up).

AliExpress triggered its bot-check (captcha 'punish' page) late in the sweep, and I stopped rather than bypass it. Prices for the screw kit, brass inserts, XT60/XT90 multi-packs, HiModel 2-12S UBEC, the MG90S 4-pack and the BMP390 variant come from search-result cards (lowest variant) only; their contents and shipping are unverified.
AliExpress prices are what a non-logged-in visitor from Korea saw. New-user-only prices (one per account) are recorded in notes; price_krw uses the regular price. Prices change often.

I have no manufacturer BMP280 noise figure. The Bosch datasheet PDF is AES-encrypted (pypdf lacks cryptography) and the Bosch product URL returned 404. Only Adafruit's vendor claim is recorded (0.25 m altitude noise, ±1 hPa).

BMP388 noise (0.03 Pa) and relative accuracy (±0.08 hPa) come from the Bosch product page as quoted in search results; my direct fetch returned 404. The MS5611 resolution table comes from the MEAS datasheet as summarized by search, not fetched directly.
Shipping fees are unknown for Mechasolution (shown only as an image), icbanq, the Bambu KR store below ₩70,000, and the AliExpress FS-i6X 500+-sold listing.
No Korean MG90S 5-pack listing found; only icbanq at 2,860 KRW each. MG90S specs come from the TowerPro manufacturer page, and clones are not verified.

No Korean ripstop fabric listing and no ready-made 1.0-1.7 m model rocket or drone parachute was found in Korea. The AliExpress parachute listing does not state fabric, gore count or shroud-line strength.
ATmega128 board listings (Korean and AliExpress) mostly omit clock, regulator and ISP header details. AliExpress boards may ship with an 8 MHz crystal (per a buyer review).

Mechasolution's 4-channel level converter and DeviceMart's SMG microSD module do not name the MOSFET or state whether there is level shifting. The DFRobot Fermion serial data logger at icbanq lists no storage type or specs.
No independently tested data (thrust, servo torque, sensor noise) was found for any clone part. All figures are vendor or manufacturer claims.
